- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤0.25), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.75) and price is trending up, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% to prevent over-optimism.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.25–0.67), model often misreads momentum; use 14-day EWMA instead of 30-day forecast for better alignment with sentiment shifts.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap), model may be overfitting to recent highs; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.
